visual.general_description: Frontal chest radiograph in cool blue-gray tones showing both lung fields, ribs, clavicles and the central spine and mediastinal shadow. Two red block arrows are overlaid, one on each side of the image.
visual.detailed_description: A frontal chest radiograph shown in blue-gray tones, cropped tightly around the thorax so the ribs fill the frame and the lower edge cuts through the upper abdomen. The shoulders and clavicles are visible at the top, with a small dark rounded object at top center over the neck region and a small partly cropped glyph at the top edge left of center. The lung field on the left of the image shows patchy, hazy areas of increased density that are more conspicuous in the mid and lower zone, while the lung field on the right of the image looks darker and more uniform. Two bright red block arrows are overlaid: one on the left side of the image pointing toward the right (toward the hazy lung field), and one on the right side of the image pointing toward the left (toward the upper-outer part of the right-of-image lung). No printed laterality marker, date, name, scale or panel letter is legible.

A small dark rounded object is present at top center and a small partly cropped glyph at the top edge.

clinical_significance.statement: The article lists the chest radiograph among the investigations on which the MDR-TB diagnosis was based.

limitations: No printed laterality marker is legible, so which anatomical side each arrow or finding lies on is a caption claim, not a pixel claim.
The caption says bilateral patchy opacities and a right-sided cavity; the cavity and the meaning of each arrow are not independently confirmed from pixels, and the arrows carry no printed legend.
No diagnosis is made from the appearance.
